review_contract: Select only distinct, concrete direct or indirect loss-of-user-or-protocol-assets root causes supported by the PDF and exact vulnerable code.

findings.reason: Incorrect content-type header key; body and state are unchanged, with no asset impact.
Missing context cancellation can delay or leak retrieval work; no permanent asset lock is established.
Unclosed gRPC connections can exhaust descriptors and impair availability only.
Nil cleanup after connection creation failure can crash the client; no asset movement or lock.
Unbounded path input creates memory denial of service, not a demonstrated permanent asset lock.
A zero reservation window can panic the client. The report and code do not demonstrate misbilling or unauthorized asset movement.
Unknown chunk formats can produce error, nil data, or panic behavior; no invalid blob acceptance is shown.
Wrong-length commitment keys reach storage lookup/error handling; no cryptographic or authorization bypass.
Empty revert data maps to INTERNAL_ERROR rather than INVALID_CERT, but never maps to SUCCESS.
Mismatched security-parameter array lengths can panic; no invalid certificate is accepted.
Unchecked uint32-to-uint8 conversion may truncate representation, but Merkle and security checks remain and no bypassing certificate or asset loss is established.
A non-secret query value is printed; no asset authorization or value is exposed.
Explicitly enabled admin routes toggle only predefined dispersal backends; the report provides no concrete asset-loss sequence.
Unsupported quorum values encounter the on-chain limit rather than bypass it; cited assets are outside the strict scope.
RPC failure returns an internal error and requires retry/failover; verification does not fail open.
Five general comments have no direct security implications or asset-loss mechanism.
